page.title: Restore point retention
page.description: How long backup restore points are kept, and which objects follow their own rule.

noTenant.title: No tenant selected
noTenant.description: Choose a tenant to manage its retention policies.

forbidden.title: Administrators only
forbidden.description: Retention shapes what backup data survives at all, so only tenant and provider administrators can view or change it.

empty.title: No retention policy yet
empty.description: Without one, every restore point is kept. Recommended: {rule}.

form.description: Choose how long restore points are kept. The newest restore point of an object, and its only checked one, are never removed, whatever the policy says.
form.name: Name
form.tiersHint: Each tier covers an age range. "Keep every one" never thins it; a number of days keeps only the newest restore point per that many days. The last tier can stay open-ended (kept without an age limit) or end, after which nothing survives.
form.tierKeepEveryDays: One per {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
form.previewTitle: What the next run would remove
form.previewHeld: {count, plural, one {# restore point is} other {# restore points are}} held by a legal hold and stay
form.previewNone: Nothing would be removed with this policy.
form.previewRefused: Fix the policy above to see a preview.
form.previewError: The preview could not be loaded.

problems.object_not_found: That object does not exist in this tenant.
problems.object_already_scoped: That object already has its own retention policy.
problems.default_exists: This tenant already has a default policy; edit it instead.
problems.empty: At least one tier is required.
problems.start: The first tier must start at day 0.
problems.from_days: A tier's start must be a whole number of days.
problems.keep_every_days: "Keep every N days" must be 0 or a positive whole number.
problems.to_days: A tier's end must be later than its start.
problems.open_ended: Only the last tier may have no end.
problems.gap: Tiers must be contiguous, with no gap or overlap.
problems.required: A custom policy needs at least one tier.
problems.generic: This policy could not be saved as entered.

confirm.deleteDescription: "{name}" will no longer prune restore points. Nothing already pruned comes back.
confirm.deleteDescriptionOverride: "{name}" stops governing its objects; the tenant default applies to them from then on, which may prune more. Nothing already pruned comes back.
confirm.stricterDescription: With this policy, the next retention run would remove {count, plural, one {# restore point} other {# restore points}}. This cannot be undone.

dashboardWidget.title: Restore point retention
dashboardWidget.description: How long backup restore points are kept, and which objects follow their own rule.
dashboardWidget.recommendedDefault: No policy yet, so every restore point is kept. The recommended default policy: {rule}.
dashboardWidget.thinningNote: Restore points in between are thinned to save space; not every one is kept.
dashboardWidget.keepAll: Everything is kept: there is no retention policy yet, so no restore point is ever pruned.
dashboardWidget.keepByAge: Every restore point is kept; the policy sets no age limit.
dashboardWidget.prunes: Restore points older than {days} days are pruned; the newest {keepLast, plural, one {restore point} other {# restore points}} of each object are always kept.
dashboardWidget.onlyOverrides: There is no tenant default, so objects without their own policy keep every restore point. {count, plural, one {# object follows} other {# objects follow}} its own policy, which may prune its restore points.
dashboardWidget.emptyWithPolicy: The retention policy applies once restore points exist.
